result.classification: Short hot historical-row query diagnostics; no saturation/capacity winner
limits: Both tables share one backend and both sink paths remain active/idle. This does not compare independent databases.
Small repeated 64-row working set, ten discarded warmup queries, no OS cache eviction or physical cold-read claim.
Only 100 measured queries per cell; p99 is a small-sample observation, p99.9 unavailable.
Queries use one synchronous worker with 200ms think time per pair; wall rates are offered-load-limited, not capacity.

volumes.scope: non-atomic owned-volume snapshot, no shared-filesystem double count

environment.cotenancy: Only this order CDC pipeline; no other heavy lab.

limits: Sample-window deltas exclude startup and exit outside observation. Decreasing counters are treated as restarts and the new counter is accumulated; reset intervals have no CPU utilization estimate.
Short-lived actors may be missed; use native pre-exit cgroup counters as well.
CPU utilization is interval-average percent of one core; short spikes may be missed.
Docker disk bytes are not device I/O latency; absent counters are unavailable, not zero.

Current source hashes identify the curated checkout, not historical failed binaries; per-process logs preserve exact build manifests.
Million-row trials used a 600-second checkpoint timeout/minimum pause 0; final SQL explicitly sets 120 seconds/1 second and requires a separate final-configuration lifecycle smoke test.
Resource observations are sample-window scopes; native I/O snapshots are cumulative per-container and include background work. Do not add these scopes together.
Native ZSTD/LZ4 codec ratios, physical I/O latency/queue depth and power-loss durability are unmeasured.
Source CSV gzip reference is a different layer from native database/wire compression.
No global exactly-once/linearizability proof or competitive capacity winner.
